style: Say very slowly, softly and gently, in a calm, soothing voice, like a kind teacher leading young children through a calm-down breathing exercise
lines: Hi, I'm Shelly. Which calm tool shall we try?
Hands on your belly. Let's fill our balloons.
Breathe in.
Breathe out.
Well done. How does your body feel now?
Point your finger at the red dot. Follow it around the star.
You traced the whole star! Five slow breaths.
Let's count slowly, in a whisper.
Now back down, even slower.
All done. Take one more slow breath.
Stand up tall, with space around you.
Reach up high, like you are picking a star.
Arms up, and lean slowly to one side. Now the other side.
Curl up small like a turtle in its shell. Breathe slowly.
Roll your shoulders up, back and down. Slowly.
Squeeze your hands into fists. Squeeze, squeeze. Now let go, and wiggle your fingers.
Nice stretching! Sit down slowly and take a breath.
Five things you can see. Look around slowly. A window? A blue crayon? Your shoes?
Four things you can feel. Your feet on the floor. Your shirt. The chair. Your hands on your knees.
Three things you can hear. Close your eyes and listen. The clock? Birds? Someone breathing?
Two things you can smell. Sniff gently. Your sleeve? A pencil? If you can't smell anything, that's okay.
One big slow breath. Breathe in slowly... and let it all out.
Great noticing!
You are here, right now. Well done.
How does your body feel right now?
How does your body feel now, after our calm tool?
Our bodies feel calmer than before. That tool helped!
Our bodies feel about the same. That's okay. We can try another tool.
Sometimes we need a little more time. Let's try another tool.
